title: Influencers and Trust
text:
Social media influencers have become powerful voices in modern advertising. Brands often pay them to promote products to millions of followers, because audiences tend to trust recommendations from people they feel they know. Influencers can reach younger consumers more effectively than many traditional television channels.

Nevertheless, the practice raises questions about honesty. When a post does not clearly reveal that it is sponsored, followers may believe that the recommendation is independent. For this reason, many countries now require influencers to disclose paid partnerships openly.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why do brands pay influencers?
options: Because influencers are cheaper than all other media
Because audiences tend to trust recommendations from people they feel they know
Because followers never buy products without a celebrity
Because television channels no longer exist

questions.text: What do many countries now require influencers to do?
options: Pay a fee to each brand
Remove all sponsored posts from their accounts

questions.text: What can be inferred about sponsored posts that do not clearly say they are paid?
options: They may mislead followers into thinking the recommendation is independent
They are usually more honest than other posts
They are banned in every country

questions.text: Why might influencers be more persuasive than traditional advertising?
options: Their followers feel a personal connection with them
They are required by law to be popular
They always speak about several products at once

vocabulary.definition: people who have many followers on social media and can affect what others buy or think
to advertise or support something in order to increase its popularity or sales
to make information known that was previously private or hidden
paid for by a company in return for promotion

paragraph_translations: Influenciadores das redes sociais tornaram-se vozes poderosas na publicidade moderna. As marcas frequentemente pagam para que eles promovam produtos a milhões de seguidores, porque o público tende a confiar em recomendações de pessoas que sente conhecer. Os influenciadores conseguem alcançar consumidores mais jovens de forma mais eficaz do que muitos canais de televisão tradicionais.

No entanto, essa prática levanta questões sobre a honestidade. Quando uma publicação não revela claramente que é patrocinada, os seguidores podem acreditar que a recomendação é independente. Por isso, muitos países agora exigem que os influenciadores divulguem abertamente as parcerias pagas.
